ENGINEERING INSPECTION REPORT
Date of Inspection: February 10, 2026
Property: 789 Industrial Blvd, Minneapolis MN

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
The low-slope commercial roof system was inspected following reports of interior water damage after a prolonged snow event in January 2026. The EPDM membrane system exhibited ponding water and evidence of snowmelt infiltration. Some wind-driven displacement of snow was noted on the windward parapet edge. Our inspection focused on the membrane condition, drainage pathways, and ice dam formation along the north parapet.

FINDINGS:
We observed standing water in three locations on the roof surface, indicating negative drainage conditions. Ice dam formation was present along the north parapet where snowmelt refroze. The membrane seams near the drainage obstruction area showed signs of stress. Snow load accumulation was significant during the January event.

Minor wind damage was observed on the parapet cap flashing where sustained wind had lifted one section. However, the primary water intrusion path follows the snowmelt and ponding water pattern, not the wind-affected area.

CONCLUSION:
The observed damage is the result of long-term deterioration of the membrane system and deferred maintenance of the drainage system. The ponding water and snowmelt infiltration are consequences of inadequate slope and clogged drains, not the weather event. The wind damage to the parapet cap is incidental and unrelated to the interior water damage. We recommend the building owner address the drainage deficiencies and replace the membrane as part of routine maintenance.
